touches.text: Outline check: when a ticket is cast, the cheapest model reads it beside the outline sections it touches. A conflict, or an open question in those sections, becomes a question on the ticket, which holds its build until answered. It reads the outline as it stands each time, so editing the outline costs nothing.

A ticket's plan carries only what a door can check. A decision line's by (free prose, census 2026-09-16: 70 of 70) is not checked and not kept: the cast door checks writes_to and reads, and by goes. Who authored a line is not tracked (Akien 2026-10-28: "there is no point in tracking the 'authoring entity'", except a gate-pass certificate). CC's decision, 2026-11-13, on Q#96 (ticket d421051bc1f7, child C), after Akien: "we are moving away from prose. that's why the tickets became json ... we need things we can check. and that does mean you have to create adjudications. but i'd say this one isn't working."

A rule not yet enforced is made into a ticket now. Akien 2026-11-13, on Q#89: "i said no ious because you were making a lot of them. ious have to be made into tickets. if we have them floating around, then they need to be made tickets NOW." So ticket f5dbfddea8c6 makes the rewrites it proposed at the 24 remaining sites (CLAUDE.md, MAP.md, the press office, PROOF.md). Where a site names a rule whose physics is not built, it names that rule's real ticket id, cast now if none exists; the word "ticket" with no id behind it does not count. CC's reading of his answer, on a mechanism CC made.

More than one builder runs at a time, so work is kept apart by branches: each ticket's work on its own branch, named by the ticket id, merged locally with git, no pull request (GitHub is hosting only). WHY: "the best way to manage scaling is branches."
